executive_summary: Michael (an autonomous fleet seat) currently has zero sending capability -- confirmed absent, not blocked (44 files under scripts/michael/, zero SMS/email transport calls). Chairman ratification 561878ae (amending b9d3607e) authorizes exactly one narrow, capped, revocable exception to the flat 'Michael never sends SMS/email' rule: a four-times-daily (6am/10am/2pm/6pm ET) personal-domain checkpoint text to the chairman, and nothing else. A pre-build security-agent baseline (verdict: acceptable-with-controls) produced 7 MUST controls (FR-1..FR-7) plus a SHOULD (FR-8); this SD's own VALIDATION pass at LEAD-TO-PLAN (sub_agent_execution_results 1171f9c8) resolved each control's concrete mechanism, and a subsequent TESTING pass at PLAN-TO-EXEC (sub_agent_execution_results id captured below) measured and disproved the original FR-8 census route (ADDITIONAL_SCOPE would FAIL the ratchet, not pass it -- proven by a live probe), found a real fail-open edge in partial-identity handling (H4), found two pinned registry tests that break by construction and were unlisted (H3), and found the original all-unit test plan could not satisfy the SD's own 'demonstrated BY A RUN' exit predicate (H2). This PRD folds all TESTING findings in as binding requirements/decisions before EXEC starts. Delivered: a new DB-backed ledger + enable/disable row (with an ephemeral-PG DDL test proving the constraints pre-chairman-apply), an additive identity parameter on the existing Twilio provider (all-three-or-null, no partial-identity fail-open), a new closed-verb script following the house scripts/michael/*.mjs pattern, Task-Scheduler wiring reusing the existing multi-window FEEDERS registry, and KNOWN_DEBT census registration (not ADDITIONAL_SCOPE) for the new chairman-reaching sink.

functional_requirements.title: Same-day cap of 4, fail-closed on BOTH read-failure branches
functional_requirements.description: Before sending, read a same-day count of outcome='sent' rows for the ledger, for IN-WINDOW send attempts only (see FR-6 for the attempt definition). A schedule firing twice, a hand re-run, or a duplicate trigger must all be refused past the 4th accepted send. lib/michael/db.mjs's readRows() returns {rows:[],tables_absent:true} on a missing relation AND {rows:[],error} on any other read error -- BOTH yield an empty array, which reads as "0 sent today" and fails OPEN unless the verb explicitly branches on tables_absent OR error and refuses in either case (mirror scripts/michael/todoist-act.mjs:73-77's two-branch preflight). TESTING-verified: this two-branch shape correctly mirrors todoist-act.mjs (TESTING C13).
acceptance_criteria: A 5th in-window send attempt in one ET date is refused with a distinct code (CAP_EXCEEDED), no external call made, a ledger row recorded
A simulated ledger-read error (tables_absent=true) refuses the send with TABLES_ABSENT, never proceeds as if 0 were sent
A simulated ledger-read error (error set, tables_absent=false) refuses the send with READ_FAILED, never proceeds as if 0 were sent

functional_requirements.title: Immutable recipient, hash-pinned as TAMPER-EVIDENCE (not secrecy)
functional_requirements.description: The recipient is never accepted from a CLI parameter, DB row, or an alternate env override. The real chairman number is read from process.env.CHAIRMAN_PHONE (the existing repo-wide convention; no literal E.164 goes into git), and the RAW resolved string's sha256 must match a hardcoded module constant before any send is attempted -- refusing on any mismatch (RECIPIENT_HASH_MISMATCH), including a mismatch caused by incidental formatting drift (whitespace, missing +). PER TESTING M9: hash the RAW env string, not a normalized form (do NOT route through lib/solomon/chairman-sms-exchanges.js's phoneKey(), which strips to the last-10-digits and would accept a different-country number sharing them). This mechanism is TAMPER-EVIDENCE / unredirectability, not secrecy -- a phone-number sha256 is only ~1e10 candidates and is trivially offline-enumerable, so the PRD makes no secrecy claim about the constant.
acceptance_criteria: Passing any alternate recipient via CLI flag has no code path to reach the send call
A CHAIRMAN_PHONE value whose RAW-string sha256 does not match the pinned constant refuses the send (RECIPIENT_HASH_MISMATCH), no external call made
A CHAIRMAN_PHONE value differing ONLY by surrounding whitespace also refuses (proves raw-string hashing, not silent normalization)
A code read confirms zero parameter/row inputs feed the recipient

functional_requirements.title: Messaging identity isolated via an additive optional parameter on the shared provider -- ALL THREE fields or null, never partial
functional_requirements.description: Extend lib/messaging/providers/twilio-provider.js's send()/isConfigured() with an optional `identity` parameter: {accountSid, authToken, messagingService}. When supplied, sid/token/messagingService are read ONLY from it, never falling back to process.env. TESTING H4 (MEASURED): the existing isConfigured() checks only accountSid()+authToken() (twilio-provider.js:35-37) and messagingService() is read UNGUARDED at :59 -- so a partial identity (sid+token set, messagingService unset) would make a REAL authenticated POST to Twilio with an empty MessagingServiceSid, a fail-OPEN edge inside a capability whose entire premise is fail-closed. FIX (binding): lib/michael/checkpoint-identity.mjs returns the identity object ONLY when ALL THREE of MICHAEL_TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID/MICHAEL_TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN/MICHAEL_TWILIO_MESSAGING_SERVICE are non-empty -- any subset returns null, and the verb then refuses closed exactly like the fully-unset case. send()'s own identity-branch validation must independently also require all three (defense in depth against a caller bypassing the resolver). TESTING M5: statusCallbackUrl() (:26, :63-64) reads the SHARED process.env.TWILIO_STATUS_CALLBACK_URL regardless of identity -- a Michael-identity send would register Adam's webhook as the callback target, where signature verification uses the shared authToken() and would always fail for a Michael-signed callback (fail-closed, not a security hole, but persistent cross-lane noise). FIX (binding): when identity is supplied, OMIT the StatusCallback form field entirely (Michael has no delivery-callback receiver; unconditionally registering one is the actual bug). Adam's chairman-sms-gate continues calling send() with no identity argument and is untouched (3 existing callers: api/webhooks/twilio-sms.js, lib/chairman/sms-bridge.js, lib/chairman/sms-outbound-worker.js -- zero call-site changes, TESTING/VALIDATION-verified). A parallel/duplicate provider module was rejected (VALIDATION V-6): it would exit scripts/lint/transport-test-isolation-guard-lint.mjs's frozen GUARDED_FILES list and tests/unit/outbound-sink-conformance.test.js's TRANSPORT_TARGETS census. TESTING vacuous-pass warning (C13): twilio-provider.js:48 shouldRefuseRealSend() short-circuits under VITEST before the identity branch UNLESS the test explicitly vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...) -- every FR-3 test MUST stub fetch or it passes without ever exercising the identity code path.
acceptance_criteria: send({identity: {...}}) never reads process.env.TWILIO_* when identity is supplied

A partial identity (any 1 or 2 of the 3 MICHAEL_TWILIO_* vars set) resolves to null from checkpoint-identity.mjs and the verb refuses closed -- zero external calls, proven by a test with fetch stubbed (not vacuously passing via the test-env guard)
An identity-bearing send omits the StatusCallback form field entirely
Existing callers (sms-bridge.js, sms-outbound-worker.js, twilio-sms.js webhook) pass no identity argument and are behaviorally unchanged (regression-tested)
Unsetting only MICHAEL_TWILIO_* env vars fails Michael's send while an Adam chairman-SMS send in the same process succeeds unaffected

functional_requirements.title: Template-only body, never raw personal text, with an as-of freshness pointer
functional_requirements.description: The checkpoint body is composed from a fixed template plus booleans and counts only -- pulled from existing michael_* count-producing tables (calendar-read, gmail-triage, todoist-brief), never raw mail/calendar/health/household text. Matches the existing brief assembler (scripts/michael/brief-assemble.mjs) convention of composing from counts and already-redacted rows. TESTING M8: the producing feeders run at 04:00-05:30 / 12:00-12:30 / 18:00-18:30 ET (lib/michael/feeder.mjs:35-43), so the 10:00 checkpoint would otherwise carry counts up to ~4.5h stale and the 18:00 checkpoint races the SAME-window producers and usually carries noon data -- a checkpoint that READS as current but is not. FIX (binding): the body includes an as-of pointer (the producing run's timestamp/et_date, not the send time), so a stale count is visible as stale rather than silently implied fresh.
acceptance_criteria: The body-composer function's inputs are limited to numeric/boolean values plus the producing run's as-of timestamp -- no free-text parameter reaches the template
A test asserts the composed body reflects the actual producing run's as-of value, not the checkpoint's own send time
A code/test inspection confirms zero raw-text fields (mail subject/body, calendar title, health metric text) are interpolated into the message

functional_requirements.title: Dedicated Michael-local enable/disable row, read fresh, fail-closed
functional_requirements.description: A new, dedicated table michael_checkpoint_send_enabled (singleton row, natural key 'checkpoint_send') is read with NO cache on every send attempt, failing closed (treated as disabled) on tables_absent, a read error, or a missing row. leo_feature_flags was rejected (VALIDATION V-4: 30s cache, fails OPEN, and CLAUDE.md rule 12 binds specific flags there to chairman ratification, too heavy for a lightweight toggle). michael_rules.auto_apply was rejected (VALIDATION V-5: flipping an active rule off requires an Opus-verifier artifact, too slow for 'revocation is a row flip'). A dedicated table keeps this SD self-sufficient (no dependency on the staged-unapplied chairman_switchon_policy migration) and revocable by a simple UPDATE.
acceptance_criteria: Disabling the row (enabled=false) causes the next in-window send attempt to be held/refused, no external call, a ledger row written
A simulated read failure on the enable table is treated as disabled (fail-closed), not enabled
Re-enabling the row allows the next in-window send to proceed normally
Proven at the ephemeral-PG DDL tier that the table's RLS/REVOKE grants match the michael_* convention (service_role only)

functional_requirements.title: Every IN-WINDOW attempt writes a ledger row, redacted; out-of-window fires and dry-runs write no row
functional_requirements.description: TESTING L11 (contradiction found): the original wording ('every attempt -- sent, held, or refused -- writes a ledger row') directly contradicted TS-1's dry-run expectation of no row, and TESTING M6 separately found the schedule fires ~96x/day (15-min interval) of which only 8 fall in-window, with no defined behavior for the other ~88 -- risking ~32k rows/year with no retention story if written, or a silently-wrong FR if not. RESOLVED DEFINITION (binding): an 'attempt' is an IN-WINDOW invocation that passes the window gate (lib/michael/feeder.mjs's own inWindow/windowIdFor). Out-of-window fires return inert with NO ledger row and NO external call (matching every other Michael feeder's existing inert-outside-window convention). A --dry-run invocation, even in-window, writes NO ledger row (matches the dry-run-by-default convention every Michael verb follows). Every OTHER in-window, non-dry-run attempt -- sent, held, or refused -- writes exactly one row to michael_checkpoint_send_ledger at-or-before the external call, storing only sha256(body) and body length (never the verbatim body), mirroring todoist-act.mjs's redactCall/SEC-M3 convention.
acceptance_criteria: An out-of-window invocation is inert: no ledger row, no external call
A --dry-run in-window invocation writes no ledger row
A capped in-window, non-dry-run attempt writes a ledger row with outcome='refused' and a refusal_code
A held (disabled) in-window, non-dry-run attempt writes a ledger row with outcome='held'
A sent attempt writes a ledger row with outcome='sent', body_sha256, body_len, and provider_message_id -- never the raw body text

functional_requirements.title: Per-slot deduplication key, proven at the DDL tier
functional_requirements.description: Each of the 4 daily ET windows (6am/10am/2pm/6pm) has its own dedup identity so a re-run inside an already-sent window cannot double-send it. Reuses lib/michael/feeder.mjs's existing windowIdFor(minuteOfDay, window) -- the window's own `start` string IS the per-slot key -- plus a DB-level UNIQUE (et_date, window_slot) WHERE outcome='sent' constraint as defense-in-depth. TESTING H2: the constraint's existence cannot be proven by a mocked-client unit test (it can only prove the CODE handles a 23505, never that the CONSTRAINT exists) -- proof requires the ephemeral-PG DDL tier (see FR-1..FR-7's shared DDL test below), matching the repo's existing tests/ddl/michael-tables-ddl.db.test.js pattern (applies the real migration to an ephemeral vanilla PG16, no chairman apply needed).
acceptance_criteria: Two runs inside the same window on the same ET date (app-level): the second is refused (ALREADY_SENT_THIS_WINDOW), no double external call
At the ephemeral-PG DDL tier: a concurrent double-insert for the same (et_date, window_slot) sent row is independently rejected by the DB constraint, not merely by application logic

functional_requirements.title: SHOULD reuse existing gate checks + dry-run-by-default; MUST register via KNOWN_DEBT (not ADDITIONAL_SCOPE) in the outbound-sink census
functional_requirements.description: SHOULD reuse the existing gate's quiet-hours/no-secrets/length checks and the dry-run-by-default convention every Michael verb follows (a bare run without --apply/--live never calls the provider). CORRECTED (TESTING H1, MEASURED): the original plan to register via ADDITIONAL_SCOPE was WRONG and disproven by a live probe -- ADDITIONAL_SCOPE puts a path IN the scanned scope, and since the new verb reaches lib/messaging/providers/twilio-provider.js WITHOUT reaching lib/adam/should-consult-solomon.js's CONSULT_GATE, it lands in nonConformant, which tests/unit/outbound-sink-conformance.test.js:256 asserts toEqual([]) -- so ADDITIONAL_SCOPE registration makes the RATCHET TEST FAIL, not pass. Routing through CONSULT_GATE was considered and rejected as semantically wrong (Solomon-consult is an Adam-lane governance check, not fitting a personal 4x/day checkpoint). BINDING DECISION: register scripts/michael/checkpoint-send.mjs into the file's KNOWN_DEBT allowlist with a linked_ref citing this SD, and raise KNOWN_DEBT_CEILING from 9 to 10 (line ~124, whose comment reads 'Never raise this') AND update the pinned expectation at line ~292 (expect(KNOWN_DEBT_CEILING).toBe(9) -> toBe(10)) in the SAME PR -- the file's own comment calls this 'a one-line ratchet kill', making it a deliberate, reviewable exception rather than a silent bump. This is the chairman-ratified, capped, narrow exception the KNOWN_DEBT allowlist exists to hold.
acceptance_criteria: tests/unit/outbound-sink-conformance.test.js passes with the new verb registered in KNOWN_DEBT (not ADDITIONAL_SCOPE), KNOWN_DEBT_CEILING raised 9->10, and the corresponding pin updated in the same PR
The default (no --apply) invocation never calls the Twilio provider

functional_requirements.title: Cross-seat dependency: encode ratification 561878ae into the live Michael contract
functional_requirements.description: The authorizing ratification 561878ae is UNENCODED (encoded_at/encoded_ref both NULL, verified live query). CLAUDE_MICHAEL.md:127 currently carries only its predecessor b9d3607e's text, ending 'Neither tier is built or scheduled and this clause authorises no build.' Per the single-scribe convention, scribe_seat=adam-49eabb23 owns this encode, not this build -- already signaled to the coordinator (worker-signal 6249c0d4, severity high) as a named cross-seat dependency to land before/alongside this SD's completion, covering all 4 contract sites the carve-out under-scopes (CLAUDE_MICHAEL.md :36, :56, :61, :62), not just section 4. functional_requirements.title: A missed window is accepted as silent (no reconciliation gauge in this SD's scope)
functional_requirements.description: TESTING M7: lib/michael/feeder.mjs:241 returns inert('outside_et_window') with no row if the host is asleep/hibernating through both fire-minutes of a window (each window offers only 2 fires at :00/:15 given the 15-min interval); scripts/setup-michael-host-tasks.mjs's own header notes no wake-from-sleep is configured. For read feeders this is survivable (an existing missing/failed-run gauge covers it in Adam's 6am brief); the checkpoint-send verb has no equivalent reader, so a missed window means the chairman simply does not get a text and nothing records that he did not. BINDING SCOPE DECISION: building a reconciliation/missed-window gauge is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this narrow SD (it would expand the capability grant beyond 'one verb, four windows, nothing else'); this limitation is accepted and documented here rather than silently discovered later. A future SD may add a daily reconciliation gauge (docs/michael/02-SPEC.md:149's michael-feeder-health pattern) if this proves to matter in practice.
acceptance_criteria: No reconciliation/missed-window-detection code is built as part of this SD (explicitly out of scope, not an oversight)

implementation_approach.summary: Migration + DDL test first (proves the schema independent of chairman apply), then the corrected additive provider parameter (all-or-nothing identity, no status-callback bleed), then the identity resolver, then the verb itself, then scheduler + registry-pin + KNOWN_DEBT-census registration, then the full test suite including the seeded-DB integration test -- each step independently testable in dry-run/fail-closed mode without live credentials.
steps: 1. Write the migration (+ _DOWN.sql, @approved-by header, DO $verify$ block) and tests/ddl/michael-checkpoint-send-ddl.db.test.js against an ephemeral PG16 (TS-13)
2. Add the migration-shape test (mirroring the 4 existing precedents)

3. Add the optional all-or-nothing identity parameter to twilio-provider.js send()/isConfigured(); omit StatusCallback for identity sends; verify the 3 existing callers are unaffected (regression test)

5. Write scripts/michael/checkpoint-send.mjs on the lib/michael/db.mjs seam: window gate (in/out), cap check (FR-1), enable check (FR-5), recipient hash-pin on the raw string (FR-2), per-slot dedup (FR-7), template+as-of body (FR-4), ledger write with the FR-6 attempt definition, dry-run-by-default
6. Add the FEEDERS registry entry (lib/michael/feeder.mjs) and update its pinned test; register the Task Scheduler task (scripts/setup-michael-host-tasks.mjs) and update its pinned test
7. Register the new verb in tests/unit/outbound-sink-conformance.test.js's KNOWN_DEBT list, raise KNOWN_DEBT_CEILING 9->10, update the pin

8. Write tests/unit/michael/checkpoint-send.test.js covering TS-1..TS-12/TS-15/TS-16, stubbing fetch per TR-7, mutation-verify the fail-closed branches (temporarily invert a check, confirm the test fails, restore)
9. Write the TS-14 seeded-DB integration test proving cap+revocation by a real run against a test-schema instance
10. Run the full regression sweep before EXEC-TO-PLAN
